tool.name: Cox Proportional Hazards
tool.description: Multivariate survival regression and hazard ratio forest plot

configfiles.configfile:
suppressWarnings(suppressMessages({ library(survival) library(survminer) }))
data <- read.delim("${input_data}", sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = TRUE, check.names = TRUE)
## Resolve column selection - data_column may pass index or name resolve_col_name <- function(data, col_value) { col_value <- trimws(col_value) col_idx <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(col_value)) if (!is.na(col_idx) && col_idx >= 1 && col_idx <= ncol(data)) { return(colnames(data)[col_idx]) } return(col_value) }
time_col_name <- resolve_col_name(data, "${time_col}") status_col_name <- resolve_col_name(data, "${status_col}") print(paste("Using time column:", time_col_name)) print(paste("Using status column:", status_col_name)) ## Covariates come from a multi-select data_column as a comma-separated list of indices covariate_values <- strsplit("${covariates}", ",")[[1]] covariate_names <- vapply(covariate_values, function(v) resolve_col_name(data, v), character(1)) covariate_names <- unname(covariate_names) print(paste("Using covariates:", paste(covariate_names, collapse = ", ")))
## Ensure status and time are numeric data[[status_col_name]] <- as.numeric(as.character(data[[status_col_name]])) data[[time_col_name]] <- as.numeric(as.character(data[[time_col_name]]))
## Note: covariates are left as-is. Numeric columns are treated as continuous ## predictors; character/categorical columns were already converted to ## factors by read.delim(stringsAsFactors = TRUE) above.
cox_formula <- as.formula(paste0( "Surv(`", time_col_name, "`, `", status_col_name, "`) ~ ", paste0("`", covariate_names, "`", collapse = " + ") ))
fit <- coxph(cox_formula, data = data)
#set $ap = $sec_appearance p <- ggforest( fit, data = data, #if str($ap.main_title).strip(): main = "${ap.main_title}", #end if fontsize = ${ap.fontsize} )
#if $output_format == "pdf": pdf("forest", width = ${ap.plot_width}, height = ${ap.plot_height}) #else: png("forest", width = ${ap.plot_width} * 300, height = ${ap.plot_height} * 300, res = 300) #end if print(p) dev.off()
#if $ph_test: zph <- cox.zph(fit) zph_table <- as.data.frame(zph\$table) write.table(zph_table, file = "ph_test.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA) #end if

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool fits a multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression model using the R **survival** package's ``coxph()`` function, and visualizes the estimated hazard ratios as a forest plot using **survminer**'s ``ggforest()``.
Unlike the companion Kaplan-Meier tool, which compares survival between groups without adjusting for other variables, this tool estimates the independent effect of each selected covariate on the hazard of the event, holding the others constant.
**Input**
A tabular file (TSV) containing at minimum:
- A **time** column (numeric survival/follow-up time) - A **status/event** column (0 = censored, 1 = event occurred) - One or more **covariate** columns to include in the model
Numeric covariate columns are treated as continuous predictors. Text covariate columns are treated as categorical (factor) predictors.
**Output**
- A forest plot (PNG or PDF) showing the hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval for each covariate. - Optionally, a table of proportional-hazards assumption test results (Schoenfeld residuals, via ``cox.zph()``), one row per covariate plus a GLOBAL row. A small p-value (conventionally < 0.05) suggests the proportionality assumption may not hold for that covariate, meaning its effect on the hazard may change over time rather than staying constant - in which case the hazard ratio from this model should be interpreted with caution.
.. class:: infomark
**note**
**Status encoding:** The R `survival` package uses 1 = event, 0 = censored by default. Some datasets (e.g. `lung`) use 2 = event; recode your status column to 0/1 before running this tool if needed.
